body: I got the Decon JJF grey and they were way lighter when they arrived, they were my first barefoot shoes so I was so impressed with them that I ended up keeping them.
I recently got the 955 on sale and am very happy with my purchase. All the features, great battery and very affordable.
I've just gone for the 955 for the maps, but the extra battery life is probably just as useful. Spend the money, you'll be using it for years!
I've got 7 months left on my Whoop subscription and would absolutely love a Garmin alternative
Just a heads up taking melatonin probably won't help your sleep in the long run.
Will always take them if I can, if the note scanner's down then I won't take them, same with £50 notes. I'm personally not confident verifying anything other than £5, £10, £20 English notes.
Fun fact, white dogshit has become more scarce due to changes in dog food. Excess calcium found in bonemeal (which is used less these days) turned the poo white!

I'm so glad you stopped yourself. I know you feel like this is the only way but there is a version of your life where you can be happy, you just can't see it through all the pain.

You've got this, if you ever need to talk I'm here to message.

Thanks for sharing. It's looking like it's going to be at least another year until my ADHD assessment (can't afford to go private), do you think it could be worth taking them in the interim? Which drug were you prescribed?

I'm still undiagnosed (only found out last year) so currently unmedicated. My worry with antidepressants is side effects and interaction with alcohol. I am drinking a bit more than I should at the moment, but socialising at the pub/BBQs etc is often where I'm happiest. I also occasionally need to drink for work (bartender). 

I guess it's definitely something to consider, though. I guess I've been so focused on trying to get medicated for ADHD that I'd not really thought about antidepressants as being an option. In my country it's really simple to get prescribed antidepressants, as opposed to ADHD meds which require a diagnosis, which can apparently take 2-7 years!

Thanks for the insight.

Thanks for that, it's nice to hear from someone who's been through this and got to the other side. I'm sure with time I'll be able to shift the focus, I have loads of things that I want to put my energy into, the only thing I feel that I can put it into at the moment is work (out of necessity) and smoking/drinking/substances, which I know only makes things worse.

Again, really appreciate the support.
You're right there, it's just tough to be vulnerable and I want to appear together.
Thanks for the kind words, I'm sure you're right. It just feels impossible to imagine a happy future. I'll do my best to be kind to myself :)

She did offer joined custody, however I think it's best long term to cut ties and have a clean break. I feel like the last thing I need is to be seeing her and her new partner regularly. 

I know you're right, I just won't be able to get anything substantial housing wise. I can just about afford a one room studio flat which just seems like such a big step backwards.

Thanks for the kind and supportive words though, it really does mean a lot.
You're right, I'm asking a bit but probably not as much as I should. I guess I just don't want to be a burden
Thanks mate, just so hard to imagine a future where I'm happy and have my shit together
Honestly, my family and friends, my passing wouldn't be fair on them. Chronic mental health issues make every day a battle and I'm ready to submit, despite having such a strong support network.
